tools.name: list_watches
tools.description: List Watches. A player prop you track, with the line or price move that should alert you.

tools.name: get_watches
tools.description: Read one of your Watches by id.

tools.name: update_watches
tools.description: Change fields on one of your Watches.

tools.name: delete_watches
tools.description: Delete one of your Watches. Cannot be undone, so confirm with your user first.

tools.name: send_feedback
tools.description: Tell the team what is missing or wrong. The team reads every one. Costs no quota.

tools.name: list_props
tools.description: Current FanDuel player prop lines and prices. Use it to answer "what is the line for <player> <stat>?" or to scan a game or league board. Each prop has line, over and under prices in American and decimal odds, status, and a move summary from open. Filter by player, stat, sport, league or event_id.

tools.name: line_move
tools.description: How a prop moved from open to now. Use it to answer "has <player>'s line moved?" or "which way is the money going?". Give a prop_id for one prop, or a player (optionally stat or event_id) for all of that player's props. Returns open and current line and prices, line_move in stat units, line_directio

tools.name: prop_history
tools.description: Every recorded state of one prop, oldest first: each line move, price move and suspension with its time, plus the move summary. Use it after list_props or line_move when you need the full path, not just open and current.

tools.name: recent_changes
tools.description: The change feed: every new prop, line move, price move and status change after a cursor, oldest first. Use it to keep up with the market without rereading the board. Start with since 0, then pass back meta.next_cursor each time. Optional league filter.

tools.name: list_events
tools.description: Upcoming and live games FanDuel lists, with each game's event_id, start time, in-play flag and how many props it carries. Use it to find a game before calling list_props with event_id. Filter by sport or league.

tools.name: search_docs
tools.description: Search the FanDuel API docs, guides and answers. No key. Returns ids for fetch_doc.

tools.name: fetch_doc
tools.description: Read one doc from search_docs in full, by id or URL. No key.

tools.name: search
tools.description: Search FanDuel API docs and answers. The search shape ChatGPT connectors use. No key.

tools.name: fetch
tools.description: Fetch one FanDuel API doc by id from search. The fetch shape ChatGPT connectors use. No key.

tools.name: get_sample_props
tools.description: Up to 10 real FanDuel player props, delayed like the free plan, so you can check fit before signup. No key.

tools.name: describe_signup
tools.description: What agent signup needs and its limits. No key.

tools.name: start_signup
tools.description: Start a key for your user. Ask them for their email and what they are building; never guess. They approve an emailed link (signing in first if the email already has an account); then call finish_signup.

tools.name: finish_signup
tools.description: Collect the key after your user approves the email. Poll every interval seconds. The key is returned once: store it as FANDUEL_API_KEY.

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "list_events" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: Upcoming and live games FanDuel lists, with each game's event_id, start time, in-play flag and how many props it carries. Use it to find a game before calling l…

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "search" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "fetch" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "finish_signup" references sensitive artifacts (api_key). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

evidence.snippet: Collect the key after your user approves the email. Poll every interval seconds. The key is returned once: store it as FANDUEL_API_KEY.

findings.title: Toxic flow: untrusted input can reach an external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: fetch_doc · Public sink: send_feedback, start_signup, finish_signup · Destructive: delete_watches.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: fetch_doc · Public sink: send_feedback, start_signup, finish_signup · Destructive: delete_watches

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
